newsitem.title: UK: New x-ray technique saves lung cancer lives - trial.
newsitem.headline: New x-ray technique saves lung cancer lives - trial.

text.p: A team of British researchers said on Friday that a new radiotherapy technique could greatly increase the survival rate of people with lung cancer.

They said the method, which involves intensifying x-ray therapy over a shorter period of time than usual, increased the survival rate of people with non-small-cell lung cancer from 20 percent after two years to 29 percent.

Dr Mahesh Parmar of the Medical Research Council's Cancer Trials Office in Cambridge and colleagues compared standard radiotherapy treatment with a new method known as continuous hyperfractionated accelerated radiotherapy (CHART).
Half the 550 patients in the trial were given standard radiotherapy, which involves 30 treatments over six weeks, for a total dose of 60 Gray units.
The other half got CHART, which involves 36 treatments over 12 days, with a total dose of 54 Gray.
Reporting in the Lancet medical journal, they said 29 percent of the CHART patients were still alive two years later compared with 20 percent of patients who got standard treatment.
"More people die of lung cancer than any other kind of cancer in the developed world, and the disease is rapidly on the increase in the third world," Parmar said in a statement.
"This means that making CHART the standard treatment for non-small cell lung cancer could prolong the lives of thousands of people."
Researchers are now checking the effects on CHART on other cancers.
